Why Dungeons & Dragons quickly became my PC game to beat
Me, my roommates, and a few friends play it table top. It's honestly a super fun.

I'm a veteran D&D player (since 1995), and I recently played a game of red box D&D with a great group of people over Google Hangouts.

I have to say, it was great fun. There is a dice roller addition to Hangouts which makes rolling privately less problematic. I'd recommend playing over the internet like this to anyone.

You really don't need anything fancy like Roll20, just some players and a webcam.

Kids these days with their dice rollers and webcams! Back in our day we used paper and scratched out characters with stubby #2 pencils. And we had to roll actual dice, with our bare hands in the snow!

You're right though, it doesn't take much to get started these days.

Those dice are heavy yo.

I still don't think you can beat sitting around a dining room table, eating pizza and having fun.

A good second option is playing over the intertubes.

I think the toughest part, and what makes ideas like this work so well, is that it is increasingly difficult to find people in your social circle willing to give D&D a try.

Not only are people's attention spans shorter, but there the entertainment market is saturated with so many other, simpler, less cerebral avenues of entertainment. The social stigma around the game is also a big hurdle.
